blocks.explanation:
Five A.M.s between two numbers make an A.P. of 7 terms.
Plan: use \(a_7 = a_1 + 6d\) to find \(d\), write everything over the bottom \(6\sqrt{2}\), and add \(d\) five times.
steps:
Given: \(a_1 = \sqrt{2}\), \(a_7 = \frac{15}{\sqrt{2}}\) (5 A.M.s in between)
To find: \(A_1, A_2, A_3, A_4, A_5\).
Method: \(\sqrt{2}, A_1, \ldots, A_5, \frac{15}{\sqrt{2}}\) is an A.P. of 7 terms; use \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) with \(n = 7\).

Set up the equation for \(d\)
\[a_7 = a_1 + 6d\]
\[\dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2} + 6d\]
Why: From the 1st term to the 7th term we add \(d\) six times.

Solve for \(d\)
\[6d = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}} - \sqrt{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{13}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[d = \dfrac{13}{6\sqrt{2}}\]
Why: Write \(\sqrt{2} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\) so both have the same bottom, then divide by 6.

Write the first term over \(6\sqrt{2}\)
\[\sqrt{2} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{12}{6\sqrt{2}}\]
Why: With a common bottom, adding \(d\) just adds 13 to the top.

Add \(d\) five times
\[A_1 = \dfrac{12 + 13}{6\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{25}{6\sqrt{2}}\]
\[A_2 = \dfrac{38}{6\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{19}{3\sqrt{2}}\]
\[A_3 = \dfrac{51}{6\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{17}{2\sqrt{2}}\]
\[A_4 = \dfrac{64}{6\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{32}{3\sqrt{2}}\]
\[A_5 = \dfrac{77}{6\sqrt{2}}\]
Why: Each new top is the previous top plus 13 (25, 38, 51, 64, 77); common factors are cancelled where possible.

Check: one more step reaches the last term
\[A_5 + d = \dfrac{77 + 13}{6\sqrt{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{90}{6\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Adding \(d\) to \(A_5\) must give the given last term, and it does.
